options.label: Day first, month in words, year in numbers, using “septiembre”
options.rule: When writing dates, write the day first in numbers, then the month in words, and the year in numbers; use the spelling “septiembre” for the ninth month. Examples: 6 de abril de 2009; 15 de septiembre de 2024; 1 de noviembre de 1990.

options.label: Day first, month in words, year in numbers, using “setiembre”
options.rule: When writing dates, write the day first in numbers, then the month in words, and the year in numbers; use the spelling “setiembre” for the ninth month. Examples: 6 de abril de 2009; 15 de setiembre de 2024; 1 de noviembre de 1990.

options.label: Use only numbers with leading zeros
options.rule: When writing dates, use only numbers, with a leading zero for values less than 10. Examples: 02.05.1997; 30.06.2000.

options.label: Use only numbers without leading zeros
options.rule: When writing dates, use only numbers, without a leading zero for values less than 10. Examples: 2.5.1997; 30.6.2000.

options.label: Month first, day in numbers, using “septiembre”
options.rule: When writing dates, write the month first in words, then the day in numbers, a comma, and the year in numbers; use the spelling “septiembre” for the ninth month. Examples: abril 6, 2009; septiembre 15, 2024; noviembre 1, 1990.

options.label: Use hyphens
options.rule: For dates in numerical form, use hyphens. Examples: 6-4-2009; 01-11-1990.

options.label: Use periods
options.rule: For dates in numerical form, use periods. Examples: 6.4.2009; 01.11.1990.

options.label: Use slashes
options.rule: For dates in numerical form, use slashes. Examples: 6/4/2009; 01/11/1990.

options.label: Write the time in words with the part of the day in parentheses
examples: las doce y cuarto (de la noche)
las ocho y media (de la mañana)
options.rule: When writing the time, write the time in words indicating the part of the day in parentheses. Examples: las doce y cuarto (de la noche); la una (de la madrugada); las ocho y media (de la mañana); las doce (del mediodía); las cinco (de la tarde).

options.label: Use 12-hour clock with am/pm
options.rule: When writing the time, use the 12-hour clock without a leading zero for single-digit hours; use a colon as a separator; indicate the part of the day with “am” or “pm”; do not use minutes for full hours. Examples: 0 am; 0:15 am; 1 am; 2:45 am; 8:30 am; 12 pm; 5 pm; 10 pm.

options.label: Use 12-hour clock with AM/PM
options.rule: When writing the time, use the 12-hour clock without a leading zero for single-digit hours; use a colon as a separator; indicate the part of the day with “AM” or “PM”; do not use minutes for full hours. Examples: 0 AM; 0:15 AM; 1 AM; 2:45 AM; 8:30 AM; 12 PM; 5 PM; 10 PM.

options.label: Use 12-hour clock with a. m. / p. m.
options.rule: When writing the time, use the 12-hour clock without a leading zero for single-digit hours; use a period as a separator; indicate the part of day with “a. m.” or “p. m.” Examples: 0.00 a. m.; 0.15 a. m.; 1.00 a. m.; 2.45 a. m.; 8.30 a. m.; 12.00 p. m.; 5.00 p. m.; 10.00 p. m.

options.label: Use the 24-hour clock with a colon
options.rule: When writing the time, use the 24-hour clock with a colon as separator. Examples: 00:00; 00:15; 01:00; 02:45; 08:30; 12:00; 17:00; 22:00.

options.label: Use the 24-hour clock with a period
options.rule: When writing the time, use the 24-hour clock with a period as a separator. Examples: 00.00; 00.15; 01.00; 02.45; 08.30; 12.00; 17.00; 22.00.

options.label: Use the currency symbol after the amount, with a space
options.rule: When writing amounts, use the currency symbol after the amount, with a space. Examples: 3 €; 5 $.

options.label: Use the ISO currency code after the amount, with a space
options.rule: When writing amounts, use the ISO currency code after the amount, with a space. Examples: 3 EUR; 5 USD.

options.label: Write the currency name in words
options.rule: When writing amounts, write the currency name in words. Examples: 75 euros; cien dólares estadounidenses; cinco céntimos.

options.label: Use the currency symbol before the amount, without a space
options.rule: When writing amounts, use the currency symbol before the amount, without a space. Examples: €3; $5.

options.label: Use the currency symbol before the amount, with a space
options.rule: When writing amounts, use the currency symbol before the amount, with a space. Examples: € 3; $ 5.

options.label: Use the ISO currency code before the amount, with a space
options.rule: When writing amounts, use the ISO currency code before the amount, with a space. Examples: EUR 3; USD 5.

options.label: Use commas for decimals, with no thousands separators
options.rule: To separate decimals, always use commas, with no separators for thousands, millions, etc. Examples: 5,90; 18,37; 799,99; 5870,33; 15870,33; 315262,99; 6234568,32.

options.label: Use commas for decimals, with periods only for radio stations
options.rule: To separate decimals, always use commas, with no separators for thousands, millions, etc., and periods only when referring to radio stations. Examples: 5,90; 18,37; 799,99; 5870,33; 15870,33; 315262,99; 6234568,32; 98.5 Todo Música.

options.label: Use periods for decimals, with no thousands separators
options.rule: To separate decimals, always use periods, with no separators for thousands, millions, etc. Examples: 5.90; 18.37; 799.99; 5870.33; 15870.33; 315262.99; 6234568.32.

rules.title: When writing numbers of 5 digits or more

options.label: Use commas for decimals and periods for thousands
options.rule: When writing numbers of 5 digits or more, use commas for separating decimals and periods for separating thousands, millions, etc. Examples: 15.870,33; 315.262,99; 6.234.568,32.

options.label: Use commas for decimals and spaces for thousands
options.rule: When writing numbers of 5 digits or more, use commas for separating decimals and spaces for separating thousands, millions, etc. Examples: 15 870,33; 315 262,99; 6 234 568,32.

options.label: Use commas for decimals, periods for thousands, and periods for radio stations
options.rule: When writing numbers of 5 digits or more, use commas for separating decimals and periods for separating thousands, millions, etc., and when referring to radio stations. Examples: 15.870,33; 315.262,99; 6.234.568,32; 98.5 Todo Música.

options.label: Use commas for decimals, spaces for thousands, and periods for radio stations
options.rule: When writing numbers of 5 digits or more, use commas for separating decimals, spaces for separating thousands, millions, etc., and periods when referring to radio stations. Examples: 15 870,33; 315 262,99; 6 234 568,32; 98.5 Todo Música.

options.label: Use periods for decimals and commas for thousands
options.rule: When writing numbers of 5 digits or more, use periods for separating decimals and commas for separating thousands, millions, etc. Examples: 15,870.33; 315,262.99; 6,234,568.32.

options.label: Use periods for decimals and spaces for thousands
options.rule: When writing numbers of 5 digits or more, use periods for separating decimals and spaces for separating thousands, millions, etc. Examples: 15 870.33; 315 262.99; 6 234 568.32.

rules.title: When writing numbers up to four digits

options.label: Use commas for decimals and periods for thousands
options.rule: When writing numbers up to four digits, use commas for separating decimals and periods for separating thousands. Examples: 5,90; 18,37; 799,99; 5.870,33.

options.label: Use commas for decimals and spaces for thousands
options.rule: When writing numbers up to four digits, use commas for separating decimals and spaces for separating thousands. Examples: 5,90; 18,37; 799,99; 5 870,33.

options.label: Use commas for decimals, periods for thousands, and periods for radio stations
options.rule: When writing numbers up to four digits, use commas for separating decimals and periods for separating thousands and when making reference to radio stations. Examples: 5,90; 18,37; 799,99; 5.870,33; 98.5 Todo Música.

options.label: Use commas for decimals, spaces for thousands, and periods for radio stations
options.rule: When writing numbers up to four digits, use commas for separating decimals, spaces for separating thousands, and periods when referring to radio stations. Examples: 5,90; 18,37; 799,99; 5 870,33; 98.5 Todo Música.

options.label: Use periods for decimals and commas for thousands
options.rule: When writing numbers up to four digits, use periods for separating decimals and commas for separating thousands. Examples: 5.90; 18.37; 799.99; 5,870.33.

options.label: Use periods for decimals and spaces for thousands
options.rule: When writing numbers up to four digits, use periods for separating decimals and spaces for separating thousands. Examples: 5.90; 18.37; 799.99; 5 870.33.

options.label: Write the symbol after the number, without space
options.rule: When writing percentages, write the symbol after the number, without space. Example: 99%.

options.label: Write the symbol after the number, with a space
options.rule: When writing percentages, write the symbol after the number, with a space. Example: 99 %.

options.label: Write “por cien” in words
options.rule: When writing percentages, write “por cien” in words. Examples: 99 por cien; diez por cien.

options.label: Write “por ciento” in words
options.rule: When writing percentages, write “por ciento” in words. Examples: 99 por ciento; diez por ciento.

options.label: Abbreviate when used with a numeral but spell out when used without
options.rule: When writing units of measure, abbreviate when used with a numeral but spell out when used without. Examples: 4 kg; algunos kilos.

options.label: Always abbreviate, with or without a numeral
options.rule: When writing units of measure, always abbreviate, with or without a numeral. Examples: 4 kg; algunos kg.

options.label: Always spell out, with or without a numeral
options.rule: When writing units of measure, always spell out, with or without a numeral. Example: 4 kilos; algunos kilos.

options.label: Spell out units with spelled-out numbers and abbreviate with numerals
options.rule: When writing units of measure, when numbers are spelled out, spell out the units; when numbers are written as numerals, abbreviate the units. Examples: 4 kg; cuatro kilos.

options.label: Don’t use a space between a numeral and unit
options.rule: For spacing for units of measure, don’t use a space between a numeral and unit. Example: 4kg.

options.label: Use a space between a numeral and unit
options.rule: For spacing for units of measure, use a space between a numeral and unit. Example: 4 kg.

options.label: Write out the unit in words
options.rule: When writing temperatures, write out the unit in words. Examples: 32 grados Celsius; 98 grados Fahrenheit.

options.label: Put the unit symbol after the number, with a space
options.rule: When writing temperatures, put the unit symbol after the number, with a space. Examples: 32 ºC; 98 ºF; 5 K.

options.label: Put the unit symbol after the number, without a space
options.rule: When writing temperatures, put the unit symbol after the number, without a space. Examples: 32ºC; 98ºF; 5K.

options.label: Use “grado” or “grados” without specifying the scale
options.rule: When writing temperatures, use the word “grado” or “grados” without specifying the temperature scale (informal tone). Examples: cinco grados; 25 grados.

options.label: Don’t put spaces between digits
options.rule: When writing telephone numbers, don’t put spaces between digits. Examples: 968476578; +491677896576.

options.label: Keep the format of the original
options.rule: When writing telephone numbers, keep the format of the original.

options.label: Use an en dash with spaces
options.rule: To indicate a range, use an en dash (–) with spaces. Examples: lunes – sábado; 2001 – 2003.

options.label: Use an en dash without spaces
options.rule: To indicate a range, use an en dash (–) without spaces. Examples: lunes–sábado; 2001–2003.

options.label: Use a hyphen with spaces
options.rule: To indicate a range, use a hyphen (-) with spaces. Examples: lunes - sábado; 2001 - 2003.

options.label: Use a hyphen without spaces
options.rule: To indicate a range, use a hyphen (-) without spaces. Examples: lunes-sábado; 2001-2003.

options.label: Use “de…a”
options.rule: To indicate a range, use “de…a” (“from...to”). Examples: de lunes a sábado; de 2001 a 2003.

options.label: Don’t separate abbreviated words
options.rule: When writing abbreviations, don’t separate abbreviated words. Example: EEUU.

options.label: Separate each abbreviated word with a period and a space
options.rule: When writing abbreviations, separate each abbreviated word with a period and a space. Example: EE. UU.

options.label: Separate each abbreviated word with a period without a space
options.rule: When writing abbreviations, separate each abbreviated word with a period without a space. Example: EE.UU.

options.label: Separate each abbreviated word with a space, without a period
options.rule: When writing abbreviations, separate each abbreviated word with a space, without a period. Example: EE UU.

options.label: Use single curly quotation marks
examples: Me ha dado el ‘ok’ para venir mañana
Los eventos más ‘random’ de la semana
options.rule: To highlight a specific word or expression in a text, use single curly quotation marks (‘...’). Examples: Me ha dado el ‘ok’ para venir mañana; Los eventos más ‘random’ de la semana.

options.label: Use single straight quotation marks
examples: Me ha dado el 'ok' para venir mañana
Los eventos más 'random' de la semana
options.rule: To highlight a specific word or expression in a text, use single straight quotation marks ('...'). Examples: Me ha dado el 'ok' para venir mañana; Los eventos más 'random' de la semana.

options.label: Use double curly quotation marks
options.rule: When using quotation marks, use double curly quotation marks (“…”).

options.label: Use double straight quotation marks
options.rule: When using quotation marks, use double straight quotation marks ("…").

options.label: Use guillemets
options.rule: When using quotation marks, use guillemets («…»).

options.label: Use double curly quotation marks and alternate with single curly quotation marks
options.rule: Use double curly quotation marks for quotes and alternate with single curly quotation marks for nested quotations (“ ‘ “ ” ’ ”).

options.label: Use double straight quotation marks and alternate with single straight quotation marks
options.rule: Use double straight quotation marks for quotes and alternate with single straight quotation marks for nested quotations (" ' " " ' ").

options.label: Use guillemets, double curly quotation marks, and single curly quotation marks
options.rule: Use guillemets («…») for quotes, double curly quotation marks (“…”) for quotes within quotes, and single curly quotation marks (‘...’) for further nested quotations.

options.label: Use a colon
options.rule: After a salutation, use a colon (recommended standard). Example: Buenos días:.

options.label: Use a comma
options.rule: After a salutation, use a comma. Example: Buenos días,.

rules.title: Use of the passive voice
rules.rule: Use the active voice and avoid the passive voice whenever possible.

rules.title: Capitalization
rules.rule: Don’t write words or complete texts in capital letters, except for acronyms or certain brand names. Examples: ONU; AVE.

options.label: Don’t make changes to quoted material
options.rule: When writing textual quotations, don’t make changes to quoted material.

options.label: Edit quoted material to adhere to linguistic standards
options.rule: When writing textual quotations, edit quoted material to adhere to linguistic standards.

options.label: Never use an acute accent
options.rule: When writing “solo”, never use an acute accent. Examples: Solo faltan dos horas; ha venido solo.

options.label: Put acute accent on the adverb to differentiate it from the adjective
options.rule: When writing “solo”, put an acute accent on the adverb to differentiate it from the adjective. Examples: Sólo faltan dos horas; ha venido solo.

options.label: Use the inclusive form “elle(s)”
examples: le amigue de mi compañera vive cerca
options.rule: When referring to a person of non-binary gender, use the inclusive form “elle(s)”. Examples: elle es licenciade; elles son mis amigues; le amigue de mi compañera vive cerca.

options.label: Use the inclusive form “ellx(s)”
examples: lx amigx de mi compañera vive cerca
options.rule: When referring to a person of non-binary gender, use the inclusive form “ellx(s)”. Examples: ellx es licenciadx; ellxs son mis amigxs; lx amigx de mi compañera vive cerca.

rules.title: If the gender of a group is not specified or is mixed

options.label: Use double expressions to indicate both masculine and feminine genders
examples: te has registrado como usuario/a premium
los/las participantes se reunirán esta tarde
options.rule: If the gender of a group is not specified or is mixed, use double expressions to indicate both masculine and feminine genders. Examples: los alumnos y alumnas; te has registrado como usuario/a premium; los/las participantes se reunirán esta tarde.

options.label: Use the standard masculine plural
examples: Los médicos se ocuparon del tratamiento
options.rule: If the gender of a group is not specified or is mixed, use the standard masculine plural. Example: Los médicos se ocuparon del tratamiento.

options.label: Always opt for neutral nouns and adjectives
options.rule: If the gender of a group is not specified or is mixed, always opt for neutral nouns and adjectives. Examples: la(s) persona(s); la ciudadanía.
